## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The discourse redefines the traditional Brahmanical concept of threefold knowledge by setting forth the three higher knowledges (*tevijjā*) that characterize a true brāhmaṇa in the Buddha's sense of the term. All secondary literature passages retrieved in the reference dossier pertain exclusively to the homonymous *Tevijja Sutta* of the *Dīgha Nikāya* (DN 13) rather than to this *Itivuttaka* discourse.

 Parallels outside Pali include several Chinese translations of the *Dharmapada* and related texts (T 210.35, T 212.34, T 213.33), Sanskrit recensions of the *Udānavarga* (UV 33, UVS 33), and resembling passages in the Gāndhārī *Dharmapada* (G-Dhp 1–50) and *Therīgāthā* (Thig 4.1).

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog data.*
